I’ve farmed these 30 mu in Quzhou for 40 years now. I only finished primary school, but I know my land better than any book. I rent some plots from relatives and neighbors, so altogether I have 20 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and 10 mu in stevia. My son and his wife work in a factory over in Handan, so it’s mostly me and my wife doing the day-to-day work, though I hire people with machines at harvest and planting time when it’s busy.

I don’t change what works. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 kg per mu, the maize gave 600 kg per mu, and the stevia dried to about 300 kg per mu. The stevia buyer already called to say he’s coming again this autumn, so I keep that 10 mu.

For wheat, I plant the improved seed everyone in the village uses — I forget the name, I just tell the dealer “the red bag, same as last year.” I rotary till in October before planting. Base fertilizer is one full 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind. Then I irrigate four times: winter water, jointing, heading, and filling. At jointing I spread half a bag of urea per mu, and another half bag at heading. The dealer told me that’s enough nitrogen. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once when the dealer says rust might come. Some neighbors spray three times, but twice was fine for me last year and I save money.

For maize, there is no time to plough after wheat harvest in June — the season is too short. I hire the no-till seeder to drill the hybrid seed straight into the wheat stubble the day after harvest. I put 40 kg of compound per mu down with the seed, then side-dress 25 kg of urea at the big trumpet stage. Three irrigations: right after sowing, big trumpet, and filling. Two pesticide sprays for armyworm and other bugs. No-tillage saves me days and diesel money.

Stevia is different. I plough those 10 mu fine in April and plant the improved seedlings. The dealer warned me that stevia doesn’t like too much nitrogen or the sweetness in the leaves drops, so I only put 30 kg of compound per mu at planting and top-dress once with 15 kg of urea. It drinks a lot of water, especially in July, so five irrigations. Three pesticide sprays because the buyer checks the leaves — dirty or spotted leaves and he cuts my price.

Fertilizer is more expensive this year, but I’d rather spend the money than risk a bad harvest. I thought about trying that new seed the dealer pushed, but my neighbor tried it last year and got no better yield. I’ll stick with what I know.
